stages.ix_title: Spell words with final consonant patterns: ng, nk
stages.choice_rule: Four unique whole-word spellings of one target word. Exactly one is correct and ends in ng or nk. Tier 1 wrong choices drop a letter or change one letter so the ending is not ng or nk. Tier 2 wrong choices swap ng with nk, spell nck, or double the final letter. Tier 3 wrong choices are near misses only, including a real word that swaps g with k, an extra letter, or nck. Never use IPA, a slash sound, or a bare phoneme.

gold_items.stem: A bird does this with a song.
This color is like light red.
This man has a gold crown.
Wash the dish in this at home.
My dad can put coins in this place.
We sing this together at school.
We eat a hot breakfast early on this day.
<NAME> will use the brain in class today.

roots: Give four choices and exactly one correct spelling. The correct word ends in ng or nk.
Wrong choices are attempts at that same word, not a random list of other words.
Tier 1 wrong choices drop a letter or change one letter so the ending is not ng or nk.
Tier 2 wrong choices swap ng with nk, spell the ending nck, or double the last letter.
Tier 3 wrong choices stay one small change away, including a real word that only swaps g and k.
Do not put the correct spelling in the stem. The clue is home, school, food, pets, play, family, or weather.
Choices are whole spellings. Never use IPA, a slash sound, or a single phoneme.
No brand names and no real personal names. Use <NAME> when a stem needs a child.

tier_rules.1: Four to seven words. A common one-syllable word such as sing, king, or pink. Wrong choices are obvious missing or changed letters, not real ng or nk neighbors.
tier_rules.2: Six to eight words. Wrong choices swap ng and nk, use nck, or double the final letter. The clue fits only one word.
tier_rules.3: Eight to ten words. Use <NAME> or a two-syllable word such as morning. Every wrong choice is a near miss, and one of them swaps ng with nk.
